name: Are drought-tolerant landscapes less appealing than traditional gardens?

mainEntity.name: Are drought-tolerant landscapes less appealing than traditional gardens?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, drought-tolerant landscapes can be incredibly diverse and aesthetically rich, often offering unique beauty that traditional gardens cannot. They feature a wide array of textures, colors, and forms from plants like succulents, ornamental grasses, and native shrubs. With thoughtful design, these landscapes can achieve vibrant visual interest year-round, requiring less water and maintenance while supporting local ecosystems. The perception that they are barren or plain is a common misconception.
acceptedAnswer.description: Drought-tolerant landscapes are not less appealing; they offer diverse beauty with unique textures, colors, and forms, requiring less water and maintenance.
